analysis: This PR is docs-only: it adds docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md and an 'Add-on hold' section in docs/reference/configuration.md. No executable code changes, so no direct regression in the threat model's assets or boundaries. Reviewed the hold.v1 contract it documents. It is a local AF_UNIX socket (0600, in a 0700 runtime dir) with 8 KiB line framing, a connection cap of 8, a 300 s idle timeout, and lease bounds of 30-600 s. Every request is peer-verified by LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit token: UID match, SecCodeCopyGuestWithAttributes, a code requirement pinning team SLDQ2GJ6TL and identifier io.darkbloom.sandbox, and hardened runtime. Verifying per request defends against exec-after-connect. DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY is described as not compiled into release builds, and neither env var is passed through the LaunchAgent. The docs state that the provider and add-on share a user and the socket is not a boundary against that user, and they cite TB-012. The supplied canonical context index has no TB-012 definition (the index lists TB-002/003/007/009/010/011), so the cross-reference may be dangling or the model entry may not yet exist for this new add-on boundary. That is a documentation gap to confirm, not a finding. The implementation sources (AddonIPC.swift, AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonPeerPolicy.swift, AddonHoldPaths.swift) are not in this batch, so I could not verify the documented claims: the 'live socket never taken over' behavior, the ownership.lock probe, and that DEV_IDENTITY is compiled out of release builds. The hold's effect on admission and availability (draining, the model switch) also remains unverified against code. A later pass should check the code against the docs, plus the TB-012 entry and whether the add-on hold's effect on provider admission (DoS by a signed add-on, T-057-like availability) is modeled.
